_purpose: The vocabulary of what mcgyvr can be asked to do. Each entry states what accepting it promises (`guarantee`), which family of the ladder it may start on (`starts_on`), and what evidence a contract of that type must carry (`required_evidence`). This file is the only definition: adding a task type is an edit here, not a code change. See data/README.md for how the vocabulary was validated and what was removed from it.

vendored_from._note: The starting vocabulary was inherited from local-ai's triage map. It was inherited, not validated. `excluded` below records what did not survive validation and why.

families.name: deterministic
families.doc: Tools. A program executes the change; no model is asked and no tokens are spent. Exactly one attempt, because a tool fails identically on retry.

families.name: local
families.doc: Models served by a source needing no credential. The keyless install runs here with the deterministic gate as its whole acceptance bar.

families.name: api
families.doc: Models served by a source needing a credential. The dearest family, and the one the north star measures spend against.

_families_note: Ordered cheapest to dearest, per ADR-0001 boundary 3. A family is the ladder-independent way to say where work starts: rung names are chosen by whoever wrote the config, so a catalog that named rungs would only be valid on the machine it was written for. A family resolves against any ladder — a rung is `api` when its source declares an `api_key_env` and `local` when it does not.

evidence_kinds.name: gate
evidence_kinds.doc: The deterministic acceptance gate. Carried by every type; it is the floor, not a choice.

evidence_kinds.name: tool_idempotent
evidence_kinds.doc: Re-running the tool that produced the change produces no further change. Available only to the deterministic family, where a tool owns the output.

evidence_kinds.name: references_resolved
evidence_kinds.doc: Every reference the index resolved was updated. What the index could not resolve — dynamic access, reflection, strings — is reported as unhandled rather than assumed absent.

evidence_kinds.name: no_semantic_change
evidence_kinds.doc: The parsed structure is unchanged apart from the region the type is allowed to touch. A structural check, so the gate can judge it without running anything.

evidence_kinds.name: type_check
evidence_kinds.doc: The project's type checker passes on the changed target.

evidence_kinds.name: tests_pass
evidence_kinds.doc: The contract's acceptance commands pass in the sandbox.

evidence_kinds.name: failing_test_first
evidence_kinds.doc: An acceptance command that demonstrates the defect — it must fail before the change and pass after. Without it a fix is indistinguishable from a plausible edit.

task_types.name: format
task_types.guarantee: The target is byte-identical to what the project's own formatter produces. No semantic change, and nothing is decided that the formatter's configuration did not already decide.
task_types.warrant: structural — the project's formatter is the definition of the correct output, so there is nothing for a model to be better at.
task_types.doc: Reformat existing code with the project's own formatter.

task_types.name: import_sort
task_types.guarantee: Imports are ordered as the project's own tool orders them, with no other change to the file.
task_types.warrant: structural — same argument as `format`; the tool's configuration is the specification.
task_types.doc: Order imports with the project's own tool.

task_types.name: lint_fix
task_types.guarantee: Every autofix the project's linter applies is applied, and nothing else is. A diagnostic the linter will not fix itself is explicitly out of scope for this type rather than handed to a model under the same name.
task_types.warrant: structural — the linter decides both what is wrong and what the fix is.
task_types.doc: Apply the project linter's own autofixes.

task_types.name: rename_symbol
task_types.guarantee: Every reference the index resolved is renamed, across every file that holds one. References the index could not resolve are reported, not silently left behind.
task_types.warrant: structural — the index (#47) already resolved the references, so this fans across files without a model. It is the only multi-file type in the catalog, and it is deterministic for exactly that reason.
task_types.doc: Rename a symbol across the files that reference it.

task_types.name: docstring
task_types.guarantee: Docstrings change and nothing else does — the gate compares the parsed structure and rejects a reply that edited code while claiming to document it.
task_types.warrant: measured, weakly — prose about code already present is the cheapest thing a small worker is asked for, and `no_semantic_change` makes a wrong answer detectable without running anything.
task_types.doc: Write or correct a docstring for one named target. Prose about existing behaviour, so it is cheap but not mechanical.

task_types.name: type_annotation
task_types.guarantee: Annotations are added to the named target and the project's type checker accepts the result. The checker, not the worker, decides whether the inference was right.
task_types.warrant: structural — the acceptance evidence is a checker's verdict rather than a judgement, so a wrong answer is caught rather than argued about.
task_types.doc: Add type annotations to one target.

task_types.name: function_implementation
task_types.guarantee: One function is implemented against the interface the contract states, and the contract's acceptance commands pass.
task_types.warrant: measured — this is the shape HumanEval+ actually measures (short, self-contained function synthesis against a stated signature), so the capability table's ordering is a usable proxy for it. It is the only type of which that is true.
task_types.doc: Implement one function against a stated interface. The canonical single-target model task.

task_types.name: test_scaffold
task_types.guarantee: Tests are written for one named target against its stated interface, and they pass. The target itself is outside the contract's scope, so a worker cannot make a test pass by changing what it tests.
task_types.warrant: structural — the scope boundary removes the failure mode that makes generated tests worthless, and it is enforced by the gate rather than asked for in a prompt.
task_types.doc: Write tests for one named target against its stated interface.

task_types.name: bug_fix
task_types.guarantee: Defined wrong behaviour in one target is corrected, demonstrated by a command that fails before the change and passes after.
task_types.warrant: structural, not measured — the capability table ranks synthesis against a given signature and says nothing about diagnosis in a repository the model can see (data/README.md), so nothing here warrants the diagnostic step. What makes a cheap attempt safe to make anyway is `failing_test_first`: with a demonstration required up front, a worker that did not understand the defect produces a change that visibly fails rather than a plausible one that lands.
task_types.doc: Correct defined wrong behaviour in one target, with a test that demonstrates the correction.

excluded.name: comment_addition
excluded.reason: No acceptance evidence distinguishes a good comment from a bad one, or from no change at all. Where the comment is a docstring the gate can at least assert nothing else moved, and that type exists; a bare comment leaves the gate with nothing to judge.

excluded.name: string_literal_edit
excluded.reason: An exact edit at a known location is an operation the deterministic tier should perform outright, not a kind of work to route. It belongs to #81 as an edit primitive; as a task type it would spend a model rung on something no model is needed for.

excluded.name: config_edit
excluded.reason: The gate's structural checks are Python and JS/TS only (ADR-0001 boundary 8). A YAML or TOML change has no adapter, so acceptance would rest on nothing but the file still parsing — too thin a bar for a file that decides how everything else runs. Revisit when an adapter covers the format.

excluded.name: multi_file_refactor
excluded.reason: Structurally unservable, not merely hard: the worker output protocol is one file's complete content in one fenced block (#25), so no model rung can emit a coordinated multi-file change at all. Routing it optimistically would guarantee a failure at the parse step rather than at the gate. `rename_symbol` is the one multi-file operation the catalog carries, and it is deterministic precisely because the index resolves the references instead of a model guessing them.

excluded.name: algorithm_implementation
excluded.reason: Not a distinct guarantee. The contract already carries the interface and the acceptance commands, so this differs from `function_implementation` only in how hard the prompt is — and difficulty is what the ladder escalates over, not a name in the vocabulary.

excluded.name: simple_bug_fix
excluded.reason: Encodes difficulty in the type name. Difficulty is already routing state, held by risk classification (#16) and resolved by escalation (#24); a second copy in the vocabulary is a copy that can disagree with the first.

excluded.name: complex_bug_fix
excluded.reason: Same as `simple_bug_fix` — difficulty is not a type.

excluded.name: interface_design
excluded.reason: No acceptance evidence exists for it. A designed interface has no command that can fail, so the deterministic gate cannot accept it and a model verifier would be the only judge — which spends expensive tokens to decide whether expensive tokens were well spent, and inverts the north star. Design is the calling agent's work; mcgyvr owns what is below the contract (ADR-0001).
